title: Massively Parallel AIG Resubstitution
problem: Resubstitution is a computationally expensive circuit restructuring algorithm that is a bottleneck in logic optimization flows for large-scale designs. Traditional sequential implementations cannot efficiently explore the vast search space of possible AIG transformations.
motivation: Accelerating resubstitution enables faster high-quality circuit optimization, yielding better area and delay characteristics in large-scale hardware designs.
method: The algorithm tests many equivalent circuit transformations in parallel on a GPU instead of one at a time, exploring far more possibilities than sequential processing allows. It works on And-Inverter Graphs (AIGs)—compact representations of digital circuits using AND gates and inverters. The main challenge is that circuits contain feedback loops (cyclic dependencies) and parallel processors may try conflicting changes; the algorithm solves this through specialized techniques for detecting and ordering these safely. It chains together with other GPU-accelerated algorithms in a synthesis sequence called resyn2rs.
key_novelty: Handling feedback loops (cyclic dependencies) and conflicting changes in parallel And-Inverter Graph resubstitution enables GPU acceleration without quality loss.
contributions: Massively parallel GPU-based AIG resubstitution algorithm with cyclic dependency management
Conflict resolution techniques for concurrent circuit restructuring operations
41.9-50.3× speedup over ABC and mockturtle sequential baselines
GPU-based resyn2rs sequence with 46.4× speedup and improved area/delay metrics

metrics.speedup: 41.9× vs ABC, 50.3× vs mockturtle, 46.4× for resyn2rs vs ABC
